findings.title: Removing findMany and changing condition return types breaks existing consumers
findings.body: The public `findMany()` method was removed and replaced with `getBaseConditions()`. Because this is an exported service and this PR only updates its tests, any existing caller of `InsightsBookingService.findMany({ select, where, ... })` will fail to compile. The return types of `getAuthorizationConditions` and `getFilterConditions` also changed from Prisma where inputs to `Prisma.Sql`, which breaks consumers that pass them to Prisma model methods or merge them as objects. Either retain a query method that uses raw SQL internally or update all consumers in the same PR.

findings.title: Public options type makes teamId optional and silently returns no rows when it is missing
findings.body: The new `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` type declares `teamId?` for every scope. The constructor passes that type through to the schema `safeParse`, but if `scope: 'team'` is supplied without `teamId`, validation fails and `this.options` is silently set to `null`; `getAuthorizationConditions` then returns `1=0`, yielding an empty result with no error. The previous discriminated-union type made this a compile-time error. Use the discriminated union or derive the public options type from the schema so missing `teamId` is caught.

findings.title: Org scope drops individual bookings when organization has no child teams
findings.body: `userIdsFromOrg` is populated only when `teamsFromOrg.length > 0`. For an organization with no child teams, `teamsFromOrg` is empty, so the second authorization branch for individual (`isTeamBooking = false`) bookings is omitted. Org owners/admins therefore cannot see non-team bookings for an org without child teams, even though `teamIds` includes `options.orgId` and org memberships should be considered. This path is not covered by the new tests, all of which create at least one child team.

findings.title: Caching behavior is no longer tested after raw SQL conversion
findings.body: The old integration suite had explicit tests for `getAuthorizationConditions()` and `getFilterConditions()` caching, and they were removed rather than converted. The service still has `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions` and now caches `Prisma.Sql` objects, so a regression in caching would go undetected. Add tests that call each method twice and assert the cached value is reused.
